doc: The mutation runner's own known-bad and known-good inputs (docs/TESTING.md s.9). Every `run` executes these first; if any verdict differs from must_be, the run is NOT EXECUTED, because a runner that misjudges these misjudges everything. Human-owned, like the registry.

canaries.why: a test that asserts nothing cannot kill a real break

entry.guard: canary: kappa returns 1.0 on one value (D11), judged by a test that asserts nothing

canaries.why: the same break, judged by a test that checks it

entry.guard: canary: kappa returns 1.0 on one value (D11), judged by a real test

canaries.why: a replacement that only adds a comment changes nothing a test could see

entry.replacement: return round((observed - expected) / (1.0 - expected), 4)  # changed nothing

canaries.why: an anchor inside a docstring is not code

entry.guard: canary: anchor matches only docstring text

canaries.why: an anchor that occurs more than once is refused (D19)
a break that stops the test module importing is not a catch

entry.guard: canary: kappa renamed, so the fixture cannot import it

canaries.why: a test that skips on the unmutated tree can judge nothing

entry.guard: canary: the named test always skips

canaries.why: a test already failing before the break proves nothing by failing after it

entry.guard: canary: the named test fails unmutated
